references.text: The preceding verse in the parable of the vineyard owner, where the first servant was sent and mistreated ([ref:Luk 20:10|Luke 20:10]). Verse 11 continues the pattern of sending another servant who is also mistreated.
Mark's parallel account where the vineyard owner sends another servant, who is also mistreated and dishonored ([ref:Mark 12:4|Mark 12:4]).

Matthew's parallel account about the vineyard owners where the servants are beaten, killed, and stoned ([ref:Matt 21:35-36|Matthew 21:35-36]). The same pattern of repeatedly sending servants and repeated mistreatment.

Historical background for the parable: God sent his messengers (the prophets) to Israel again and again, but they were mocked, despised, and ridiculed ([ref:2 Krøn 36:15-16|2 Chronicles 36:15-16]). The parable in Luke 20:11 reflects this pattern.

Jeremiah describes how God sent his servants the prophets day after day, but the people would not listen ([ref:Jer 7:25-26|Jeremiah 7:25-26]). The pattern of sending servant after servant who are all rejected corresponds to the message of the parable.
Nehemiah describes how God warned through his prophets, but the people did not listen ([ref:Neh 9:30|Nehemiah 9:30]). The parable reflects Israel's repeated rejection of God's messengers.
Stephen accuses the people of having persecuted the prophets, just as their ancestors did ([ref:Apg 7:52|Acts 7:52]). This confirms the historical pattern that the parable in Luke 20:11 illustrates.

Paul refers to them as "those who killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets" ([ref:1 Tess 2:15|1 Thessalonians 2:15]), which reflects the same pattern of persecution of God's messengers described in the parable.
